title: Sparkline playbooks and inline templates for new-project activation
creator: Marco Li
description: Design and deliver a set of compact, contextual learning artifacts (termed 'sparklines') and templated starter projects that appear in empty project canvases within the Redwood Console. The goal is to reduce first-run friction, increase template activation rate, and teach cost/rollout tradeoffs inline without requiring users to leave the console.
background: We repeatedly see new projects with 0 activity and calls to support that customers aren’t sure what to do after creating a project or model route. Existing onboarding cards are lengthy and separate from the working canvas. This initiative explores a lightweight, in-context approach: micro-playbooks (3–4 step sparklines), template snippets prewired for common use cases (chat widget, batch embedding pipeline, reranking), and a small contextual cost-preview shown before activation.
goals: Reduce time-to-first-inference for new projects to under 10 minutes (measured blue/green experiments)
Increase template activation (create-from-template) by 25% in the first 14 days
Surface cost implications inline so users understand expected per-hour or per-thousand-token cost before running large tests
success_metrics: % of users who complete sparkline steps within 7 days
Drop in support tickets labeled ‘first steps’ for Console
acceptance_criteria: Three sparkline variants implemented: Quick Chat Widget, Embedding Batch Job, Canary Rollout sandbox
Each sparkline includes a 3-step microflow with CTA wired to console actions (create route, run sample request, view cost preview)
Templates prepopulate model, prompt, and rollout policy fields; users can modify before committing
Cost preview computes a conservative estimate based on model profile and sample traffic assumptions
Figma prototypes linked and dev-ready tokens/components exported
Accessibility: all sparkline controls keyboard-navigable and screen-reader labelled
design_notes: Sparklines are compact horizontal cards anchored at the top of empty canvases; collapse to a subtle bar after completion
Use subtle sparklines (small sparkline chart) to show expected cost over 24 hours for a sample traffic pattern
Provide an expandable 'why this matters' overlay that explains batching, KV cache, and rollout implications in one paragraph
Avoid modal-heavy flows; prefer inline expansion to keep context
usability_findings: Moderated testing (n=8) — users liked the inline cost preview but wanted explicit examples for 'low traffic' vs 'bursting' assumptions
Participants confused by the term 'rollout sandbox' — renamed copy to 'canary test' in v2
Users preferred 3 steps maximum; longer flows led to drop-off
decisions: Ship three starter templates in MVP (Chat Widget, Embedding Batch, Canary Test)
Cost preview will use conservative upper-bound estimates and include a tooltip explaining assumptions
Sparkline will auto-collapse after a successful template activation and show a subtle persistent label in the header
next_steps: Finalize component tokens and hand off dev spec (Anika)
Create engineering ticket(s) to implement Sparkline host + template wiring (ENG-XXXX to be created)
Run A/B experiment targeting new projects created via self-serve to measure activation lift
